key_insight: Rarefied hypersonic surface loading over triangular protrusions has no single observability length: heat transfer is most nonlocal, pressure is moderately nonlocal, and shear is hardest to recover from bulk fields.
engineering_relevance: Design and placement of sensors or surrogates for hypersonic vehicles should account for quantity-specific nonlocal support, especially when estimating heating and shear near surface protrusions.
method: DSMC data over Mach 4–8, Kn 0.1–0.8, and three protrusion orientations
Circular neighborhoods around wall points summarized with weighted statistics, extrema, nearest-point values, and tangent-normal gradients
Region-to-point diagnostics tested against full wall profiles using R95 and surrogate/control comparisons
evidence_signal: Full-domain descriptors reduced error from 45.5% to 13.8% for Cp and from 72.6% to 12.9% for Cq, while shear improved only from 49.1% to 31.9%; heat transfer showed the clearest support near order hs.
watch_item: The observability length is quantity-dependent and geometry-dependent, so the reported thresholds may not transfer directly to other protrusion shapes or flow regimes without revalidation.
paper_title: Quantity-Dependent Bulk-to-Wall Observability of Surface Loading in Rarefied Hypersonic Flow over Triangular Protrusions
